The Pyrenees Stage Run 2025 finishes in Salardú after seven unforgettable stages Salardú (Val d’Aran), September 7th, 2025 – The Pyrenees Stage Run (PSR) came to an end yesterday after seven stages and over 200km across the Pyrenees. The participating teams crossed the finish line in Salardú in a great celebration filled with excitement,... What the runners think Barry van Oven The Netherlands, Finisher PSR2018 “Thank you for a wonderful and unforgettable week in the Pyrenees. You manage to capture the essential nature of trail-running: it’s a journey, not a race. You’re both professional and familiar, a rare combination indeed” Sergio Moya Argentina, Finisher PSR2018 “The received attentions surpass the imagined, details like waiting for the last ones and receive them like they were the first, speak by itself of the purpose imposed by the organization to make the runners happy” Albert Muñoz Spain, Finisher PSR2017 “The best organization that you can find in a race like that. Thank you so much for making us feel like a big family, without forgetting any details!” Wim Proost Belgium, Participant PSR2021 This is a stage run, far above first class: the unspoiled nature of the Pyrenees, the professional but not at all commercial organization, the passion of all you people, the hotels, the food, the trails, the unbelievable kindness of your volunteers … No other stage run can offer this passion and professionalism. Thank you so much to all of you … we Belgians are honored we could take part in this event. Tom Hoag United States of America, Finisher PSR2021 I used to think TAR was my favorite race of all time but that has been replaced by PSR. I will recommend PSR to every trail runner I know. Keep up the great work and please let everyone involved know that we thank them from the bottom of our heart! Andrew Bond United Kingdom, Participant PSR2021 Superb week for us both in such a professionally arranged event. First class throughout. Well done to you & your volunteers. You can be proud of what you have created. Stages Km Uphill Natural Parks Discover the 8 stages Route Z 8 Stages Because a stage race goes further than a one-day race. And because to get to know the Pyrenees and discover all its beauties we need at least 8 days!  Teams (2-3 runners) Because sharing it with someone is the essence of life, but also for safety. But above all, because the experience in teams goes beyond competing alone.  Marking The route will be followed with GPS + marking with ribbons and the classical marks of the GR11 which follow most of the route.  GR11 The great and classic route across the Pyrenees! We will follow the GR11 from Ribes de Freser to Salardu, with just some modifications in order to discover hidden places of the Pyrenees.  5 Natural Parks Not many races can say that its route crosses 5 Natural Parks: Capçaleres del Ter i del Freser, Vall del Madriu-Perafita-Claror, Valls del Comapedrosa, Alt Pirineu i Aigüestortes-Estany de Sant Maurici.  Accommodation and Local Dinner Different registration options: BASIC for those with the option to come with a motorhome, camper van and/or logistic support, and FULL EXPERIENCE with hotel included. Every day we will dinner all together with the awards ceremony of the stage and an audiovisual summary of the day, in order to make the experience go beyond running through the Pyrenees. This year we are celebrating the 10th edition of the PSR and the main novelty will be that we have added a stage : a festive vertical km in Encamp, after the 3rd stage! This means that the first stage will be on Saturday 29th August (one day earlier than usual), and we will finish, as always, on Saturday 5th September in Salardú. You can read the entire news HERE . The other big news will be the registration procedure: first there will be 10 days to pre-register (from the 5th to the 14th of December) , and if the limit of registered participants is reached, a lottery will be held (on the 19th of December). info@psr.run Facebook Twitter Instagram Wikiloc Facebook Twitter Instagram Wikiloc Contact Us About Us Newsletter On-line Shop · Brama Stage Run Costa Brava Stage Run | Català Español Select Page The Pyrenees Stage Run celebrates its 10th anniversary with a special edition: 8 stages and a new registration format 2 Dec 2025 The Pyrenees crossing, taking place from August 29 to September 5, 2026, debuts a festive stage in Andorra and implements a lottery system to ensure equitable access due to high demand. The Pyrenees Stage Run (PSR), the benchmark stage race in the Pyrenees, reaches its 10th edition in 2026. To commemorate a decade of adventure, the organization has announced significant changes making this edition the most special and complete in its history. The race expands to 8 stages, starting one day earlier than usual, and modifies its access system by introducing a pre-registration and lottery period. A longer and more festive PSR: The major sporting update is the extension of the route. The PSR 2026 will begin on Saturday, August 29th, one day earlier than traditionally. This change allows for the introduction of a brand new 4th stage: a Vertical Kilometer in Encamp (Andorra). This new stage, designed to be a festive day celebrating the 10th anniversary, will allow runners to enjoy two consecutive nights in Encamp, facilitating rest and social time. The competition will resume its classic format from the 5th stage (equivalent to the 4th in previous years) until crossing the finish line in Salardú on Saturday, September 5th. New registration system: Due to the sustained growth of the event and to ensure everyone has an equal opportunity to participate, the PSR is launching a new registration process. Direct registration by order is eliminated, opening a pre-registration period from December 5th to 14th, 2025. If the available spots are exceeded (130 for the Full Experience and 20 for the Basic), a lottery will be held on December 19th. This lottery will operate on a points system. In a race as international as the PSR, and considering that last year spots sold out in just two hours, the goal is to ensure equitable access regardless of the runners time zone or schedule availability. Tribute to the pioneers and the PSR Spirit”: The 10th edition will also be a tribute to the race s history. The organization has invited some runners from the 1st edition —when there were only 23 participants— to join for the first weekend, and some of them will even dare to complete the entire crossing again. The organization want this 10th edition to be a celebration of sport and friendship. The new Vertical Km in Encamp and the reunion with participants from the very first edition remind us of where we come from and everything we have built together. With the new lottery system, we want to thank our community and ensure the process is fair for everyone who dreams of crossing the Pyrenees with us.” The PSR is a stage race for teams of 2 or 3 runners that crosses the Catalan and Andorran Pyrenees, offering an experience that combines competition, tourism, and camaraderie. The race has established itself as one of the most authentic crossings on the international calendar. The Pyrenees Stage Run is organised by BiFree Sports , a company with extensive experience in organising stage races. In addition to the PSR, they also manage the Costa Brava Stage Run and the Brama Stage Run , events that stand out for offering a unique experience of adventure and challenge in spectacular natural environments. As always, the support of the technical sports clothing brand Tuga Active Wear has been fundamental, as has the institutional backing of the Patronat de Turisme Costa Brava Pirineu de Girona , contributing to the success and projection of the event.
